questions.question: What major reform did the Government of India implement to simplify workers' rights and labour law compliance in 2025?

• The reform is designed to extend **social security** and **minimum wage** protections to over **50 crore workers** in both the **organized** and **unorganized sectors**, including the burgeoning **gig economy**.

questions.question: Who among the following was appointed as the Chief Justice of India with effect from 24 November 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Justice D.Y. Chandrachud**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Justice Dhananjaya Yeshwant Chandrachud** served as the **50th Chief Justice of India (CJI)**, heading the country's judiciary for a period of **two years**.
 
• He was officially sworn in on **November 9, 2022**, and held the office until **November 10, 2024**. His appointment was made by **President Droupadi Murmu**.
 
• He succeeded **Justice U.U. Lalit**, who had a brief tenure as the **49th Chief Justice**. Justice Chandrachud's term was one of the longer ones in recent years, allowing for significant administrative and judicial reforms.
 
• He is the son of **Justice Y.V. Chandrachud**, the **16th Chief Justice of India**, who holds the record for the longest tenure in the position (**1978–1985**). This marked the first instance in Indian history of a father and son both serving as **CJI**.
 
• Prior to his elevation to the **Supreme Court** in **2016**, he served as the Chief Justice of the **Allahabad High Court** and as a judge of the **Bombay High Court**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 124 of the Constitution**: This article governs the establishment and constitution of the **Supreme Court of India**. Under **Clause 2**, every judge of the Supreme Court is appointed by the **President** by warrant under his hand and seal.
 
• **Seniority Principle**: The appointment of the **Chief Justice of India** is traditionally based on seniority. The outgoing **CJI** recommends the next senior-most judge of the **Supreme Court** to the **Union Minister of Law and Justice**, who then forwards the recommendation to the **Prime Minister** and the **President**.
 
• **Justice Sanjiv Khanna**: Following the retirement of Justice Chandrachud, **Justice Sanjiv Khanna** took the oath as the **51st Chief Justice of India** on **November 11, 2024**. He is slated to serve until **May 13, 2025**.
 
• **Master of the Roster**: The **CJI** is the administrative head of the Supreme Court and holds the exclusive power to constitute benches and allocate cases to various judges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Future Successions**: As per the current seniority list, **Justice B.R. Gavai** is expected to become the **52nd CJI** in **May 2025** and will serve until **November 23, 2025**.
 
• **Justice Surya Kant**: He is designated to take office as the **53rd Chief Justice of India** on **November 24, 2025**. This is the specific date mentioned in the query regarding the **2025** appointment. He is expected to hold the position until **February 9, 2027**.
 
• **Retirement Age**: Judges of the **Supreme Court of India** retire upon reaching the **age** of **65 years**. This is in contrast to **High Court** judges, who retire at the **age** of **62 years**.
 
• **Landmark Judgments**: During his career, **Justice D.Y. Chandrachud** was part of several historic benches, including those that decided on the **Right to Privacy**, the **Ayodhya land dispute**, and the decriminalization of **Section 377**.

questions.question: What is the maximum financial support provided for new construction of a tribal homestay unit under the Swadesh Darshan Scheme in April 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹5 Lakh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The government provides a maximum financial support of **₹5 Lakh** for the **new construction** of a **Tribal Homestay** unit to promote sustainable tourism in indigenous areas.
 
• This initiative is part of the **Swadesh Darshan Scheme** (specifically under the **SD 2.0** framework and related tribal development modules) aimed at enhancing the **Socio-economic conditions** of tribal communities.
 
• The primary objective of providing this **Financial Assistance** is to create **Livelihood Opportunities** for tribal families by allowing them to showcase their **Culture, Heritage, and Traditions** to domestic and international tourists.
 
• By **April 2025**, the guidelines emphasize that these homestays must adhere to **Sustainable Tourism** standards, ensuring minimal environmental impact while maximizing community benefits.
 
• The **Ministry of Tourism**, in collaboration with the **Ministry of Tribal Affairs**, facilitates the identification of beneficiaries, focusing on **Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs)** and other marginalized tribal hamlets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Swadesh Darshan 2.0 (SD 2.0):**
 
 
• Launched to move away from theme-based circuits toward **Destination-centric** tourism development.
 
• It focuses on **Integrated Development** of tourist destinations with a focus on **Sustainability** and **Responsibility**.
 
• The scheme encourages the **Vocal for Local** campaign by promoting indigenous crafts and stay options.
 
 
 
• **Financial Bifurcation for Homestays:**
 
 
• While **New Construction** receives up to **₹5 Lakh**, the **Upgradation or Renovation** of existing tribal houses into homestays is typically eligible for a lower subsidy, often capped at **₹3 Lakh**.
 
• This funding is usually disbursed in **Installments** based on the progress of construction and adherence to specified **Architectural Designs** that reflect local tribal aesthetics.
 
 
 
• **PM-JANMAN Connection:**
 
 
• The **Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN)**, launched in **November 2023** with a budget of over **₹24,000 Crore**, complements the Swadesh Darshan goals by improving basic infrastructure like **Roads, Electricity, and Housing** in tribal areas, making homestays more viable.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Eligibility and Implementation:**
 
 
• Beneficiaries must be **Permanent Residents** of the tribal area and possess **Valid Land Records** or certificates from local tribal councils.
 
• The **State Tourism Departments** act as the nodal agencies for the **Verification** of applications and the **Monitoring** of the construction phase.
 
 
 
• **Promotion of Niche Tourism:**
 
 
• Tribal homestays are categorized under **Niche Tourism**, specifically **Eco-Tourism** and **Ethno-Tourism**, which are seeing a high growth rate in **India** as of **2024-2025**.
 
• The scheme also provides for **Capacity Building**, where tribal hosts are trained in **Hospitality, Hygiene, and Digital Marketing** to manage their units effectively.

questions.question: Which types of equipment were included in the new defence acquisitions approved by India's Defence Acquisition Council in 2025?

options.text: Amphibious warships, missiles and swarm drones
Aircraft carriers and long-range cruise missiles
Stealth fighter jets and hypersonic glide vehicles

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amphibious warships, missiles and swarm drones**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **January and February 2025**, the **Defence Acquisition Council (DAC)**, which is the highest decision-making body of the **Ministry of Defence** in India, approved several capital acquisition proposals worth over **Rs 1.4 lakh crore** to modernize the armed forces.
 
• The approval included the procurement of **Amphibious warships**, specifically **Landing Platform Docks (LPDs)**, which are crucial for the **Indian Navy** to conduct amphibious operations, transport main battle tanks, and provide disaster relief. ***Hence, the inclusion of amphibious warships is a correct component.***
 
• The **DAC** also cleared the acquisition of advanced **missile systems**, including indigenous **Short-Range Surface-to-Air Missiles (SRSAM)** and variants of the **BrahMos** cruise missile, to strengthen the strike capability and air defense of the **Indian Navy** and **Indian Army**. ***Hence, the inclusion of missiles is a correct component.***
 
• A significant highlight of the **2025** approvals was the push for **swarm drones**. These are clusters of **Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs)** that use **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** to coordinate and overwhelm enemy air defenses or conduct mass surveillance. ***Hence, the inclusion of swarm drones is a correct component.***
 
• The entire package was designed under the **Buy (Indian-IDDM)** category, which stands for **Indigenously Designed, Developed, and Manufactured**, ensuring that the technology and production remain within **India**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Amphibious warships, missiles and swarm drones.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Defence Acquisition Council (DAC):**
 
 
• The **DAC** was formed in **2001** following the recommendations of the **Group of Ministers** on **Reforming the National Security System** after the **Kargil War**.
 
• It is headed by the **Union Defence Minister** and includes the **Chief of Defence Staff (CDS)** and the chiefs of the **Army, Navy, and Air Force**.
 
• Its primary function is to give **Acceptance of Necessity (AoN)** to various defense procurement projects.
 
 
 
• **Amphibious Operations and LPDs:**
 
 
• **Landing Platform Docks (LPDs)** are massive vessels capable of carrying **helicopters**, **landing crafts**, and hundreds of **marines**.
 
• They serve as a mobile sea base and are essential for **India's** security strategy in the **Indian Ocean Region (IOR)**, particularly for protecting island territories like the **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**.
 
 
 
• **Swarm Drone Technology:**
 
 
• **Swarm drones** represent the future of **asymmetric warfare**. They communicate via **mesh networks** and can perform "saturated strikes" that are difficult for traditional **radar** and **anti-aircraft guns** to stop.
 
• The **Indian Army** has been integrating these into its **mechanized forces** to enhance reconnaissance and offensive power along the **Line of Actual Control (LAC)**.
 
 
 
• **Atmanirbhar Bharat in Defence:**
 
 
• The **Government of India** has issued several **Positive Indigenisation Lists**, which specify hundreds of items that the **Armed Forces** must procure only from **domestic industry**.
 
• The **Defence Acquisition Procedure (DAP) 2020** further incentivizes local production and the participation of **private sector** players alongside **Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs)** like **HAL** and **DRDO**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Technology Features:**
 
 
• The **missiles** approved in **2025** feature high **precision-guidance** systems and **electronic counter-countermeasures (ECCM)** to bypass enemy jamming.
 
• The **Amphibious warships** are expected to have a **displacement** of over **20,000 tonnes** and will be built by **Indian shipyards** such as **Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL)** or **Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers (GRSE)**.
 
• **Drones** approved include **Loitering Munitions**, which act as "suicide drones," staying in the air for extended periods before diving onto a target.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Impact:**
 
 
• These acquisitions help **India** counter the growing influence of the **People's Liberation Army Navy (PLAN)** in the **Indian Ocean**.
 
• By focusing on **missiles** and **drones**, **India** is transitioning from conventional force structures to **technology-intensive** military capabilities.

questions.question: Who was awarded the Sahitya Akademi Award 2024 for his book "Ik Hor Ashwthama" in the Dogri language?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chaman Arora**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chaman Arora** has been conferred with the prestigious **Sahitya Akademi Award 2024** for his literary contribution to the **Dogri language**.
 
• He received this recognition for his book titled **"Ik Hor Ashwthama"**, which is a significant work in contemporary Dogri literature.
 
• The **Sahitya Akademi** announced its annual awards for **2024** on **December 20, 2024**, honoring writers across **24 Indian languages**.
 
• The selection for the award was made based on the recommendations of a **three-member jury** in the respective languages, following the rules and procedures laid down by the Akademi.
 
• **Chaman Arora's** work **"Ik Hor Ashwthama"** reflects deep cultural and social narratives relevant to the **Dogra community** and the **Jammu region**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sahitya Akademi Award**:
 
 
• Established in **1954**, it is a literary honor in **India** conferred annually by the **Sahitya Akademi** (India's National Academy of Letters).
 
• The award is presented to the most outstanding books of literary merit published in any of the **major Indian languages**.
 
• Initially, the award amount was **Rs. 5,000**, but it has been increased over the years and currently stands at **Rs. 1,00,000** along with an engraved copper plaque and a shawl.
 
• The Akademi recognizes **24 languages**, including the **22 languages** listed in the **Eighth Schedule** of the Constitution, plus **English** and **Rajasthani**.
 
 
 
• **Dogri Language**:
 
 
• **Dogri** is primarily spoken in the **Jammu region** of **Jammu and Kashmir**, as well as parts of **Himachal Pradesh** and **Punjab**.
 
• It was included in the **Eighth Schedule** of the **Indian Constitution** in **2003** through the **92nd Constitutional Amendment Act**.
 
• It is one of the **five official languages** of the Union Territory of **Jammu and Kashmir**.
 
 
 
• **Other Options**:
 
 
• **Shiv Kumar Batalvi**: A legendary **Punjabi poet** who became the youngest recipient of the **Sahitya Akademi Award** in **1967** for his epic verse play **"Loona"**.
 
• **Dalip Kaur Tiwana**: A renowned **Punjabi novelist** and short-story writer who won the **Sahitya Akademi Award** in **1971** for her novel **"Eho Hamara Jeevana"**.
 
• **Jaswant Singh**: While a common name, in the context of literature, **Jaswant Singh Kanwal** was a famous **Punjabi writer** who received the Sahitya Akademi Award in **1996** for his novel **"Taushali Di Hansi"**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: The 9th Asian Winter Games were held in February, 2025, with athletes from 34 countries, in:

• The competition included **6 sports**, **11 disciplines**, and **64 events**, providing a platform for top-tier winter athletes from **Asia**.

• **Future Outlook:** Following the **2025 games** in **China**, the **10th Asian Winter Games** are scheduled to be held in **Trojena, Saudi Arabia**, in **2029**, marking the first time the event will be held in **Western Asia**.
 
• **Economic Impact:** The event significantly boosted tourism in **Heilongjiang**, showcasing **China's** advanced infrastructure and its capability to host world-class sporting events following the success of the **2022 Beijing Winter Olympics**.

questions.question: The Right to Disconnect Bill, 2025, seeks to establish which principle in the modern digital workplace?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Clear work–life boundaries**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Right to Disconnect Bill, 2025**, is a legislative proposal designed to address the challenges of the **Modern Digital Workplace**, where technology often blurs the lines between professional and personal life.
 
• The primary objective of the bill is to establish **Clear work–life boundaries** by legally recognizing an employee's right to ignore work-related communications, such as **Emails**, **WhatsApp messages**, and **Phone calls**, outside of their stipulated **Working Hours**. ***Hence, option 2 is correct.***
 
• It seeks to empower **Employees** to disconnect from their work without the fear of disciplinary action or professional **Retaliation** from their **Employers**.
 
• The bill proposes that organizations must define specific **"Out-of-Office"** periods and negotiate terms of engagement that respect the **Privacy** and personal time of the workforce.
 
• This principle is aimed at tackling the **"Always-On" culture**, which has been exacerbated by the rise of **Remote Work** and **Telecommuting**, ensuring that the digital tools meant for efficiency do not lead to perpetual **Work Cycles**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Global Context and Origin**: 
 
 
• **France** became the first country to implement such a law in **January 2017**, mandating companies with more than **50 employees** to establish periods when staff should not send or receive emails.
 
• Other nations like **Italy**, **Spain**, **Ireland**, **Portugal**, and recently **Australia** (in **2024**) have introduced similar legal frameworks to protect the **Digital Wellbeing** of workers.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Mental Health**: 
 
 
• Constant connectivity is a major contributor to **Work-Related Stress**, **Burnout**, and **Mental Fatigue**.
 
• By enforcing **Work-Life Balance**, the bill aims to reduce **Anxiety** levels and improve the **Sleep Quality** of employees who are otherwise tethered to their devices **24/7**.
 
 
 
• **Productivity and Retention**: 
 
 
• Research indicates that workers who have sufficient **Recovery Time** are more **Productive**, **Creative**, and **Engaged** during their active hours.
 
• Establishing these boundaries helps in **Employee Retention** as workers feel more respected and less prone to **Exhaustion**.
 
 
 
• **Legislative History in India**: 
 
 
• In India, the concept gained traction when a **Private Member's Bill**, titled the **Right to Disconnect Bill, 2018**, was introduced in the **Lok Sabha** by MP **Supriya Sule**.
 
• The **2025 version** of the bill represents a renewed effort to modernize **Labour Laws** in the context of the **Gig Economy** and widespread **Digital Transformation**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Provisions**: The bill often includes the creation of an **Employee Welfare Committee** within companies to monitor compliance and resolve disputes regarding after-hours communication.
 
• **Exemptions**: Most versions of the **Right to Disconnect** legislation allow for exceptions during **Emergencies** or critical **Operational Requirements**, provided they are clearly defined in the **Employment Contract**.
 
• **Digital Rights**: This bill is considered a significant step in the evolution of **Digital Rights**, acknowledging that in a **Hyper-Connected** world, the right to be "offline" is essential for **Human Dignity**.

questions.question: At which event did the Vice-President of India, C. P. Radhakrishnan, deliver an inaugural address emphasizing that climate action is an opportunity, not a constraint?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharat Climate Forum 2026**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Vice-President of India**, **C. P. Radhakrishnan**, delivered the inaugural address at the **Bharat Climate Forum 2026**, which serves as a premier platform for discussing **India's** climate resilience and sustainable growth.
 
• During his speech, he emphasized that **climate action** should be perceived as a **strategic opportunity** for economic transformation and technological innovation, rather than a **constraint** or a burden on national development.
 
• The forum brought together **policymakers**, **industry leaders**, and **international experts** to deliberate on the roadmap for achieving **Net Zero emissions** while maintaining high economic productivity.
 
• **C. P. Radhakrishnan** highlighted that the transition to a **green economy** is a pathway to creating millions of **green jobs** and enhancing India's **energy security** through domestic **renewable energy** sources.
 
• He further noted that **India** is one of the few large economies on track to meet its **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)**, setting a global benchmark for **environmental leadership**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **India's Panchamrit Goals**:
 
 
• Announced at **COP26**, India's climate strategy includes reaching a **non-fossil energy capacity** of **500 GW** by **2030**.
 
• The nation aims to fulfill **50%** of its energy requirements from **renewable energy** sources by the year **2030**.
 
• A major target is the reduction of total projected **carbon emissions** by **one billion tonnes** from now until **2030**.
 
• The ultimate goal is for **India** to achieve the target of **Net Zero** emissions by the year **2070**.
 
 
 
• **C. P. Radhakrishnan**:
 
 
• He is a prominent Indian politician who has served in significant constitutional roles, including the **Governor of Maharashtra** and holding additional charges for states like **Telangana** and **Jharkhand**.
 
• Known for his focus on **administrative efficiency** and **social welfare**, his transition to the role of **Vice-President** (as per the 2026 context) underscores his continued influence in **national policy**.
 
 
 
• **National Green Hydrogen Mission**:
 
 
• Launched by the **Government of India** with an initial outlay of **Rs. 19,744 crore**, this mission aims to make India a global hub for **Green Hydrogen** production.
 
• It targets the development of at least **5 MMT** (Million Metric Tonne) of green hydrogen production capacity per annum by **2030**.
 
 
 
• **LiFE Movement**:
 
 
• The **Lifestyle for Environment (LiFE)** initiative was introduced by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** to encourage individuals to lead a life that is mindful of **resource consumption** and **waste reduction**.
 
• It promotes the concept of a **circular economy** where products are reused and recycled to minimize the **environmental footprint**.

questions.question: During the August 2025 Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) review, what revision did the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) make to its inflation forecast for FY 2025-26?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lowered to 3.1%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the **August 2025** meeting of the **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)**, the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** reviewed the domestic and global economic conditions to set the path for the upcoming quarters.
 
• A major highlight of this review was the revision of the **inflation forecast** for the **Financial Year 2025-26 (FY26)**.
 
• The **RBI** officially **lowered** the projected **CPI (Consumer Price Index) inflation** for **FY 2025-26** to **3.1%**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Lowered to 3.1%.***
 
• This downward revision from previous estimates suggests that the central bank anticipates a significant cooling of price pressures, likely due to improved **supply-side management**, stable **crude oil prices**, and a favorable **monsoon** impact on food prices.
 
• The **MPC**, led by the **RBI Governor**, emphasized that maintaining price stability is crucial for sustaining the **GDP growth** momentum of the Indian economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC):**
 
 
• The **MPC** is a **six-member** statutory body constituted by the Central Government under **Section 45ZB** of the amended **RBI Act, 1934**.
 
• It consists of **three members from the RBI** (including the Governor) and **three external members** appointed by the government.
 
• The primary objective of the **MPC** is to determine the **Policy Repo Rate** required to contain inflation within the specified target level.
 
 
 
• **Inflation Targeting Framework:**
 
 
• India adopted a **Flexible Inflation Targeting (FIT)** framework in **2016**.
 
• The **Government of India**, in consultation with the **RBI**, has set a target for **CPI inflation** at **4%**, with an upper tolerance limit of **6%** and a lower tolerance limit of **2%**.
 
• A forecast of **3.1%** for **FY 2025-26** indicates that the **RBI** expects inflation to stay well below its median target of **4%**.
 
 
 
• **Consumer Price Index (CPI):**
 
 
• **CPI** is the primary measure used by the **RBI** to monitor **retail inflation**.
 
• It tracks the change in the price of a basket of goods and services consumed by households, including **food, fuel, clothing, and housing**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Implications of the Forecast:**
 
 
• A lower inflation forecast of **3.1%** provides the **RBI** with more room to consider **interest rate cuts** (reducing the **Repo Rate**) to stimulate investment and consumption.
 
• It signals to the financial markets that the "war on inflation" is yielding results, leading to potentially lower **bond yields** and reduced **borrowing costs** for corporations and individuals.
 
 
 
• **Economic Context:**
 
 
• The **August 2025** review is a pivotal moment as it sets the expectations for the **second half of the decade**.
 
• The focus remains on the "**withdrawal of accommodation**" stance or shifting towards a "**neutral**" stance if the inflation trajectory remains consistently low near the **3.1%** mark.
 
• The **FY 2025-26** period is expected to witness the full impact of previous policy measures and global economic stabilization.
 
 
</ul
